summary: Push SIEM: real-time pseudonymized audit feed + hourly HMAC attestations and cert-rotation evidence for compliance
description: Issue summary: Customer (SatoriHealth, private deployment in a VPC) requests a push-based SIEM export that delivers near-real-time audit events to their collector with the following compliance requirements: 1) field-level pseudonymization for PII-sensitive fields (reversible tokenization only via customer KEK), 2) an hourly HMAC attestation file per batch (HMAC-SHA256) with a signed metadata manifest proving the HMAC key version and rotation window, 3) TLS mTLS client-auth between Redwood and customer's collector with guidance and proof of cert rotation, 4) chain-of-custody and retention mapping for SOC2/ISO audit. Impact: customer cannot complete onboarding for regulated workloads until evidence is provided. Environment: Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) in ap-southeast-1. Request details: - Deliver a test endpoint (push) in prod that accepts HEC-like JSON events over HTTPS with mTLS. - Provide sample mapping for Splunk HEC and Azure Sentinel ingestion (field names + examples). - Produce an example hourly attestation bundle (manifest.json + events_20260310_13.ndjson + events_20260310_13.hmac) with checkable HMAC header and RFC3161 timestamp. - Provide documentation for certificate rotation (recommended cadence, steps to upload new certs, runbook), plus a signed statement from our security team describing KMS key handling for attestation generation. Acceptance criteria: sample bundle delivered, doc pages and runbook links, and an interim workaround so SatoriHealth can start ingesting events this week.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer provides mTLS cert and IP allowlist to Support via secure channel.
2) Support provisions a push endpoint with mutual TLS in customer's VPC peering endpoint and shares the endpoint and test client cert.
3) Customer POSTs a single NDJSON event payload (sample provided below) to the endpoint.
4) Verify Redwood returns 200 and writes the event to the export staging S3 prefix with per-event pseudonymization applied.
5) At the top of the next hour, confirm that an attestation bundle (manifest + .ndjson + .hmac) is produced and pushed to the customer's S3/HTTPS destination.
sample_event_payload: Notes: 'email' is pseudonymized (tokenized) in the feed; reversible only with customer KEK.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Leah Kim (Support): Initial ticket opened after SatoriHealth submitted compliance checklist. Asking for sample bundle and runbook.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Shah (Support): Confirmed capability for per-event tokenization and that HMAC attestation is supported in principle. Requested customer KEK rotation schedule and whether they want Redwood to compute HMAC or prefer Redwood to hand off signed manifests and let the customer compute HMAC locally.

2026-03-11 - SatoriHealth (Customer): Prefers Redwood to compute HMAC using a customer-wrapped KEK (we will provide a wrapped KEK via their KMS). Need RFC3161 timestamp in manifest. Also requested demonstration bundle for auditors.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Shah (Support): Engaged infra and security. Opening INT ticket to add hourly attestation header and to support HMAC key version in manifest. See linked PR.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - Infra: current export pipeline supports NDJSON push and an 'attestor' microservice that can produce HMAC over batches. Attestor currently reads KEKs from Redwood KMS only; need to accept customer-wrapped KEK material in Private deployments.

Hypothesis: small engineering effort (~2 sprints) to add support for importing and rotating wrapped KEKs in Private control plane and to include key_version in manifest. Interim workaround: generate attestation using Redwood-managed ephemeral key, provide signed manifest + RFC3161 timestamp, and give customer an HMAC verification tool to validate against Redwood's HMAC (acceptable for initial audit evidence).

Observed: S3 upload to customer's S3 endpoint failed due to ACL/policy mismatch (403). Root cause: support account missing PutObject permission on the supplied bucket. Workaround: request customer to add redwood-inference-exporter role with s3:PutObject on prefix.
resolution: Workaround and next steps: 1) Short-term (this week): Support will provision a temporary HTTPS push endpoint with mTLS and use Redwood-managed ephemeral attestation keys to publish an example attestation bundle to an S3 prefix we control and share a signed bundle and RFC3161 timestamp with SatoriHealth for auditor review. 2) Mid-term (2 sprints): Engineering will implement support for importing customer-wrapped KEKs into the Private control plane attestor, include key_version in manifest, and add HMAC header on push exports. INT ticket INT-402 created for the engineering work; PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7123 tracks changes. 3) Ops task: provide step-by-step runbook for cert rotation and recommended cadence (90 days) and automation guidance for mounting new client certs. 4) Security will provide an attested statement about KMS handling and a scanned runbook for auditors. Customer acceptance criteria: sample bundle delivered and ability to validate HMAC using provided tool. Target ETA for full implementation: 2026-04-24.
